# Data Wrangling with dplyr dplyr is the core tool for data manipulation in R. Its verbs are organised around what they operate on: **rows**, **columns**, **groups**, or **tables**. --- ## The pipe ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Base R pipe (R ≥ 4.1) data |> filter(year == 2007) |> summarise(mean_life = mean(lifeExp)) # Tidyverse pipe (magrittr) — equivalent data %>% filter(year == 2007) %>% summarise(mean_life = mean(lifeExp)) ``` ::: --- ## Row verbs ### `filter()` — keep rows matching a condition ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Single condition gapminder |> filter(continent == "Africa") # Multiple conditions (AND) gapminder |> filter(continent == "Africa", year == 2012, lifeExp >= 70) # OR gapminder |> filter(continent == "Africa" | continent == "Asia") # %in% for multiple values years <- c(1990, 2000, 2007) countries <- c("Vietnam", "France") gapminder |> filter(year %in% years, country %in% countries) ``` ::: ### `arrange()` — reorder rows ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} gapminder |> arrange(lifeExp) # ascending gapminder |> arrange(desc(lifeExp)) # descending gapminder |> arrange(continent, desc(gdpPercap)) # multi-column ``` ::: ### `distinct()` — remove duplicate rows ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Unique rows overall df |> distinct() # Unique combinations of specific columns df |> distinct(country, continent, .keep_all = TRUE) ``` ::: ### `slice_*()` — extract rows by position ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df |> slice_max(lifeExp, n = 5) # top 5 rows by life expectancy df |> slice_min(gdpPercap, n = 3) # bottom 3 rows by GDP df |> slice_head(n = 10) # first 10 rows df |> slice_sample(n = 100) # random 100 rows ``` ::: --- ## Column verbs ### `select()` — choose columns ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # By name df |> select(country, year, lifeExp) # By position df |> select(1:3) # Helper functions df |> select(starts_with("gdp")) df |> select(ends_with("_mm")) df |> select(contains("life")) df |> select(matches("\\.t\\.")) # regex # Everything except df |> select(-country, -year) df |> select(-(col1:col4)) # Type-based selection df |> select(where(is.numeric)) df |> select(where(is.character)) ``` ::: ### `mutate()` — add or transform columns ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # New column at the end gapminder |> mutate(gdp_total = gdpPercap * pop) # Control placement gapminder |> mutate(gdp_total = gdpPercap * pop, .after = year) gapminder |> mutate(gdp_total = gdpPercap * pop, .before = 1) # Keep only used columns flights |> mutate( gain = dep_delay - arr_delay, gain_per_hour = gain / (air_time / 60), .keep = "used" ) # case_when for conditional recoding df |> mutate( age_group = case_when( age < 18 ~ "Paediatric", age < 65 ~ "Adult", .default = "Elderly" ) ) # Rename a column via rename() inside a pipeline with a new name games |> mutate( cat_label = case_when( category == "avg_us_viewers" ~ "Average US viewers", category == "rating_household" ~ "Household rating", category == "ad_cost" ~ "Ad cost (USD)", .default = as.character(category) ) ) ``` ::: ### `rename()` — rename columns ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df |> rename(new_name = old_name) df |> janitor::clean_names() # snake_case all column names automatically ``` ::: ### `relocate()` — move columns ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df |> relocate(score, .before = age) df |> relocate(id, .after = last_col()) ``` ::: --- ## Grouped operations ### `group_by()` + `summarise()` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} gapminder |> filter(year == 2007) |> group_by(continent) |> summarise( total_pop = sum(pop), median_life = median(lifeExp), mean_gdp = mean(gdpPercap), n_countries = n() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Multiple grouping variables gapminder |> group_by(continent, year) |> summarise( median_gdp = median(gdpPercap), median_lifeExp = median(lifeExp), .groups = "drop" ) ``` ::: ### Useful summary functions | Function | Description | |---|---| | `n()` | Count rows in group | | `n_distinct(x)` | Count unique values of `x` | | `mean(x, na.rm=TRUE)` | Mean | | `median(x, na.rm=TRUE)` | Median | | `sd(x, na.rm=TRUE)` | Standard deviation | | `first(x)`, `last(x)`, `nth(x, 3)` | Positional values | ### `count()` — quick frequency tables ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df |> count(group) # equivalent to group_by() + summarise(n = n()) df |> count(group, sort = TRUE) # sorted descending df |> count(group, wt = population) # weighted count ``` ::: ### `top_n()` within groups ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Counties with highest total population in each metro category counties |> group_by(state, metro) |> summarise(total_pop = sum(population)) |> top_n(1, total_pop) |> ungroup() |> count(metro) ``` ::: ### Gotcha: variable name conflicts in functions When writing functions that use dplyr verbs, avoid naming function arguments the same as column names. Use a `.` prefix convention: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # BAD: filter(year == year) matches nothing get_top_names_broken <- function(year, sex) { babynames |> filter(year == year, sex == sex) # bug! } # GOOD: prefix function arguments with . get_top_names <- function(.year, .sex) { babynames |> filter(year == .year, sex == .sex) } ``` ::: --- ## Pivoting data Tidy data has one variable per column, one observation per row, one value per cell. `pivot_longer()` and `pivot_wider()` move data between wide and long formats. ### `pivot_longer()` — wide → long ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Weekly chart positions stored in columns wk1, wk2, ..., wk76 billboard |> pivot_longer( cols = starts_with("wk"), names_to = "week", values_to = "rank", values_drop_na = TRUE ) |> mutate(week = parse_number(week)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Multiple variables encoded in column names # e.g. columns like "dob_child1", "name_child1", "dob_child2", "name_child2" household |> pivot_longer( cols = !family, names_to = c(".value", "child"), # .value tells pivot to use the prefix as the new column name names_sep = "_", values_drop_na = TRUE ) ``` ::: ### `pivot_wider()` — long → wide ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cms_patient_experience |> pivot_wider( id_cols = starts_with("org"), names_from = measure_cd, values_from = prf_rate ) ``` ::: --- ## Joins ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Left join: keep all rows from the left table flights |> left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") |> rename(airline_name = name) |> left_join(airports, by = c("dest" = "faa")) |> rename(airport_name = name) # Common join types inner_join(x, y, by = "id") # only matching rows in both left_join(x, y, by = "id") # all rows from x right_join(x, y, by = "id") # all rows from y full_join(x, y, by = "id") # all rows from both anti_join(x, y, by = "id") # rows in x not in y ``` ::: --- ## Data cleaning helpers ### Missing values ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Detect is.na(df$age) sum(is.na(df)) # total NAs any(is.na(df)) # any NAs? colSums(is.na(df)) # NAs per column # Complete cases only df[complete.cases(df), ] na.omit(df) # Replace specific values with NA df$score[df$score == 999] <- NA ``` ::: ### Dates with `lubridate` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(lubridate) ymd("2024-03-15") ymd_hms("2024-03-15 08:30:00") dmy("15/03/2024") ``` ::: ### Strings with `stringr` All `stringr` functions start with `str_` and take a string vector as first argument. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(stringr) str_trim(" excess whitespace ") # trim leading/trailing spaces str_pad("123", width = 6, pad = "0") # "000123" str_detect(x, "pattern") # logical: does the pattern appear? str_count(x, "a") # count occurrences str_subset(x, "ICU") # keep strings matching pattern str_replace(x, "old", "new") # replace first match str_replace_all(x, "old", "new") # replace all matches str_sub(x, 1, 4) # extract characters 1–4 str_length(x) # number of characters # Splitting str_split(x, fixed(" - "), n = 2, simplify = TRUE) ``` ::: ### String concatenation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # paste() default separator is a space; paste0() default is "" paste("Hello", "world", sep = " ") paste0("patient_", 1:3) # "patient_1" "patient_2" "patient_3" # str_c() from stringr: propagates NA (better for data pipelines) str_c("Hello", NA) # NA (paste() would give "Hello NA") str_c(c("a", "b", "c"), collapse = ", ") # "a, b, c" ``` ::: ### Number formatting ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} format(3.14159, digits = 3) # "3.14" format(1234567, big.mark = ",") # "1,234,567" formatC(0.001234, format = "e", digits = 2) # "1.23e-03" formatC(3.14159, format = "f", digits = 2) # "3.14" ``` ::: --- ## Practical example: babynames ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(babynames) # Trend for a single name babynames |> filter(name == "Sophie") |> ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n, color = sex)) + geom_line() # Year-normalised proportions and change over time babynames |> group_by(year) |> mutate(year_total = sum(n)) |> ungroup() |> mutate(fraction = n / year_total) |> group_by(name) |> arrange(name, year) |> mutate(ratio = fraction / lag(fraction)) |> # year-on-year growth filter(fraction >= 0.00001) |> slice_max(ratio, n = 1) ``` ::: --- ## Collapsing boolean columns into a single factor A common pattern in clinical data: you have several mutually exclusive binary columns (e.g. admission reason) and want a single factor column instead. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tmp <- data.frame( respiratory = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), 40, replace = TRUE), neurologic = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), 40, replace = TRUE), shock = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), 40, replace = TRUE) ) tmp$reason <- apply(tmp[1:3], 1, function(row) names(tmp)[which(row)]) ``` ::: --- ## Converting factors to numeric ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Convert all factor columns to numeric is_factor <- sapply(df, is.factor) df[is_factor] <- lapply(df[is_factor], function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))) ``` :::
